# Calibrated Native Marker Replay and Observation Scoring

## Scope

This chapter records the provisional software handoff from a source-bound
marker-calibration artifact through native marker forward kinematics into the
existing feedback observation scorer. It adds no calibration estimator,
native execution adapter, observation scorer, or qualification authority.

## Evidence Chain

The MuJoCo fixture starts with one immutable T01 replay bundle and executes a
full-state native replay. Native poses on the simulation-relative input grid
and a separate synthetic calibration capture produce the existing
`native-marker-calibration/1.0.0` artifact through the shared
`static_marker_offsets` estimator. The test revalidates the artifact against
the source, capture bytes, native pose history, exact clock, provider identity,
and frame/timebase declarations. A changed pose clock and tampered local
offset are rejected.

The artifact creates the existing `NativeMarkerMap`, which binds its digest.
A fresh native replay then generates marker positions through model-owned
forward kinematics. Synthetic observations with a known 1 mm vertical
difference enter the existing F09 observation-scoring path. Its score receipt
links the calibration artifact, marker map, native execution, marker output,
observations, and alignment identities. The report retains the full 17-row
required denominator, scores only the synthetic fixture, and remains
unqualified.

## Limits

The capture and model are synthetic; no private capture or production marker
attachment is included. The calibration residual is in-sample, not an
independent prediction. Digests provide integrity assertions, not signed
execution provenance. The synthetic score does not establish anatomy,
physiology, contact fidelity, held-out accuracy, or qualification.

The end-to-end scorer integration now also passes in actual Drake 1.57 and
Pinocchio 4.1 native marker-FK tests. The Pinocchio case used ordinary source
imports from a copied test module outside the checkout. The Drake SDK test
used a test-only namespace bootstrap for `src.engines.physics_engines.drake`
and its `.python` package, pointing to the real source before loading the real
provider. This bypassed the broad repository initializer, which still cannot
complete in that minimal environment because `structlog` and `simpleeval` are
missing. No native provider or physics implementation was mocked, but ordinary
public package bootstrap was not tested. The exact test setup and limitation
are recorded in the F09 turnover. OpenSim marker geometry remains
position-level and does not provide the full-state replay used by this
handoff. All production rows and independent physics and qualification gates
remain open.

## Reproduction

Run the MuJoCo case with the focused calibration, FK, and observation-scoring
tests:

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/engines/test_feedback_observation_qualification.py::test_observation_score_consumes_native_mujoco_marker_receipt
python3 -m pytest tests/unit/engines/test_feedback_marker_calibration.py tests/unit/engines/test_feedback_native_markers.py
```
